prompt: Who lives with you and shares food costs?
guidance: A CalFresh household is everyone who buys and prepares food together — not necessarily everyone on the lease. Roommates who shop and cook separately are different households even if you share a kitchen. State your numbers clearly: how many people, and which of them share food with you.

prompt: What is your monthly gross income, before taxes and deductions?
guidance: Give gross (pre-tax) earnings from all sources for everyone in your CalFresh household. If your income varies week to week, say so and offer a recent four-week average. Do not estimate downward to qualify — your county verifies with pay stubs, and any mismatch can delay or deny benefits.

prompt: How much do you earn from gig or self-employment work?
guidance: Report your gross self-employment income, then mention that allowable business expenses reduce the net amount used for CalFresh. If you drive for a platform (Uber, DoorDash, Instacart), mileage, platform fees, and gas count as expenses. CalFresh lets you choose between actual expenses or a flat 40% deduction — offer to provide a recent earnings summary from the app.

prompt: What do you pay for rent, utilities, and other housing costs each month?
guidance: Include rent or mortgage, plus separate amounts for heat, electricity, gas, water, trash, and any phone or internet bills paid by your household. California grants the Standard Utility Allowance (SUA) if you pay any heat or cooling bill separately from rent — this is usually the higher deduction, so mention any utility bill in your name.

prompt: Are you enrolled at least half-time in a college or university?
guidance: Half-time students 18-49 are ineligible for CalFresh unless they meet an exemption: working 20+ hours per week, caring for a dependent under 12, in an EOPS/CARE/CalWORKs program, in a Local Program That Increases Employability (LPTIE) — many CA community colleges qualify — or receiving certain disability benefits. State the exact exemption that applies to you, with specifics.

prompt: Are all members of your household US citizens or qualified non-citizens?
guidance: Only state the status of people who are applying. Members who are not applying do not need to disclose status. Children born in the US are citizens regardless of parent status. Some non-citizens who do not qualify for federal CalFresh may qualify for the California Food Assistance Program (CFAP) — the same benefit, state-funded. If anyone is unsure, ask to speak with a CalFresh outreach worker before answering.

prompt: Can you verify your identity? What documents do you have?
guidance: Acceptable identity proof in California includes a state ID, driver license or AB 60 license, passport, Matrícula Consular, work or school ID, voter card, or two of: birth certificate, social security card, hospital records. If you cannot produce an ID at the interview, federal rules require your county to accept a sworn statement plus a collateral contact (someone who can vouch for you) — ask about this option.

prompt: What is your current cash on hand plus this month's expected income?
guidance: Expedited (three-day) CalFresh requires household resources under $100 plus gross income under $150 for the month, OR rent and utilities greater than combined income and resources. Be precise about your cash, bank balances, and what you expect to earn this month. If you complete the interview at intake, the county can sometimes issue benefits the same day.

prompt: Has anyone moved in or out of your household since your last application?
guidance: Report every change in who shares food costs, not just lease changes. Moving in: someone joined and you buy and prepare food together. Moving out: someone left who used to share food costs. Even temporary changes (a sibling staying for a month) should be mentioned if they affect food sharing. In California you can report changes anytime via BenefitsCal.com, by phone, or in person at your county office.
